symptom: `create microflow Tmp.F returns Boolean as $b begin … return $b; end;` still produced three errors after the parentheses hint landed — "missing '(' at 'returns'" (with the hint), "missing ':' at 'Boolean'" and, three lines into the body, "extraneous input 'return' expecting the start of a statement"; a bare `$l: List of Tmp.Item` gave "missing ')' at 'returns'" as a second error, `create nanoflow M.NF begin end;` three. The report asked for one message.
cause: The hint only annotated ANTLR's first error; the cascade came from recovery itself. ANTLR inserts the `(`, parses `returns` as a parameter name (parameterName admits keywords), lets dataType's recovery swallow `Boolean as $b begin declare … true` and closes the statement at that `;` — so the tail of the body is reported at program level, outside the statement the hint fired for.
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLMicroflow.g4 (createMicroflow/Nanoflow/RuleStatement: `(LPAREN microflowParameterList? RPAREN | microflowParameterList)?`); mdl/visitor/visitor_microflow.go (refuseRoutineHeaderWithoutParens); the regex hint in visitor.go removed
insight: Dump the error listener's rule-context stack at each error before choosing where to fix a cascade: here the third error's stack was just ProgramContext, i.e. the parser had already closed the statement, so no per-line or per-statement suppression in the listener can tie it back to the hint — the recovered parse no longer knows where the real statement ends. Accept-then-refuse removes the cascade at its source: the grammar parses the bare header only so the builder refuses it, which gives one error, positioned at the token the `(` should precede, and lets the builder quote the user's own header back with the parentheses added. The previous fix's note ('suppressing it would need cross-error state') was the tell that the listener was the wrong layer. Two controls: stubbing the refusal makes the test fail with 0 errors (the grammar alone would silently ACCEPT a new spelling), and the original code fails it with the reported three. Same pattern as the positional call argument (#569). When removing the old hint, check the surviving case — a bare header with a second, unrelated error on its line — would otherwise get the explanation twice.
